To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed and used an antibody that selectively recognizes monomer-misoldeed SOD1 and have shown that monomer-misfolding of SOD1 precedes the clinical onset of symptoms in ALS mouse models and in an individual with an SOD1 mutation.
we have identified a unique antibody that recognizes misfolded SODE1 in three different mouse models of ALS and in a human with an SOD1 mutation.

a structure-guided strategy was used to develop an antibody selective for monomer-misfolding of SOD1 in amyotrophic lateral sclerosi (ALS) and that the antibody was shown to be useful in identifying monomer-misformed SOD1 in the motor neurons of three mouse models of SOD1-ALS, as well as in the human disease, and that this misfolding was found to precede and accompany motor neuron loss in the ALS mouse models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an antibody to pathological misfolded SUD1 in ALS.
the development of a novel SOD1 antibody that recognizes only misfolded Sod1 and its application to the study of SOD1 misfolding in mouse models of SOD1 ALS and a human patient.
the identification and characterization of an immunological epitope that selectively recognizes pathological monomer-m isfolded SOD 1 in ALS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
misfolded Sod1 is present in the motor neurons of Sod1 mutant ALS mouse models, and in the motor neurons and spinal cords of an individual with an AAV mutation.
misfolded SODE1 can be detected in ALS mice and in a patient with an SOD1 mutation, and this misfolded SDE1 is associated with degenerating motor neurons.
the SEDI antibody is a valuable tool for the identification of monomer misfolded Sod1 in the ALS models and patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
misfolded Sod1 is a biomarker for ALS.
we developed an antibody that recognizes monomer-missfolded SOD in the SOD ALS mouse models and in a human patient with SOD1 ALS.

we have discovered a novel antibody that recognizes misfolded monomeric forms of SOD in ALS and we have used it to show that misfolded monomer SOD1 accumulates in motor neurons before symptoms and decreases at the end stage, concomitant of motor neuron loss.
The main takeaway from our work is that
misfolded Sod1 is present in the motor neuron cytoplasm of Sod1 ALS mice and in the motor neuron of a human with ALS.
misfolded Sod1 can be detected in ALS mice and in human patients with ALS and that it is a useful marker for disease progression.
monomer-misfolding of SOD1 is a hallmark of ALS.
